label: (all iia labels)
summary: iia magnitudes in layer B are not on a common scale, so the magnitude_continuity check of assertion verification is UNUSABLE for iia assertions (27 of the 158 assertions the legacy bare-label tier was hiding, including the tier's largest, serbia|iia|1920-1944 at 573 rows). Measured on consolidated_layer_b.parquet (26,175 iia rows, 164 labels, 1909-1945), median wheat production in 'tonnes': canada 756,867; denmark 690,589; sweden 497,275; germany 293,228; france 101,145; united kingdom 96,525; serbia 14,618; netherlands 1,103. Denmark and Sweden are plausible for the interwar period; France (~8 Mt), Germany (~4-5 Mt), Canada (~10-14 Mt) and the Netherlands (~150 kt) are one to two orders of magnitude low, so the error is per-table, not a single global factor that could be divided out. Area is affected too: median wheat area in 'ha' 1930-1938 is russian federation 125,800, serbia 58,000, czech republic 5,000 - the USSR/Serbia ratio is 2.2 where the real one is ~90. Within one series the scale also flips: serbia wheat area is 58,000 ha for 1934 and 17,000 ha for the 1934-1938 average. Audit required: trace the unit column and any multiplier applied per iia publication/table during layer_b consolidation. Until then, iia assertions must be verified on scope/vintage/documentary grounds only and a verifier must not read iia staple_magnitudes as evidence of reporting scope. No polity or territorial action follows from this row. AUDIT DISCHARGED 2026-08-20, AND EVERY LEG OF THE DIAGNOSIS ABOVE IS REFUTED. The entry asked to 'trace the unit column and any multiplier applied per iia publication/table during layer_b consolidation'. Done: of all 12,052 layer-B iia `tonnes` rows, 10,810 (89.7%) carry a value that appears VERBATIM among the raw extract's production values for the same year, and only 112 (0.9%) need a power-of-ten factor to find a raw match -- x10 29, x100 49, x1000 34, which is the size of the already-confirmed iia-tobacco-implausible-magnitudes / iia-hops-x100 / iia-1933-x10-wrong-volume-cells classes rather than a new one. A per-table rescaling during consolidation would produce a LOW verbatim rate; 90% is incompatible with it. THE MAGNITUDE EVIDENCE WAS A WRONG-ITEM COMPARISON. Both legs cited `wheat`, and iia-wheat-is-spelt-and-meslin (confirmed, logged later) establishes that the iia `wheat` item is spelt and meslin -- the raw extract carries ZERO wheat production rows. Against raw spelt+meslin the layer-B medians are the SAME series, not one to two orders low: canada 756,867 vs 771,015; denmark 690,589 vs 745,022; sweden 497,275 vs 502,537; france 101,145 vs 97,650; uk 96,525 vs 87,906 (uk: england and wales). Those are plausible magnitudes for the crop they actually are -- Danish and Swedish blandsaed, French meteil, Canadian mixed grain -- and the Netherlands' 1,103 t, flagged here as absurd for wheat, is unremarkable for a minor mixed grain. THE AREA RATIO IS CORRECT IN LAYER B. This entry reads the USSR/Serbia area ratio as 2.2 'where the real one is ~90'; ~90 is a WHEAT ratio. For spelt+meslin the comparable raw quantity is the per-year SUM of the two products, and its medians give ussr 157,150 ha against yugoslavia 79,000 ha, a ratio of 1.99 -- so layer-B's 2.2 is right. (A first pass at this refutation reported 4.44 by taking the median of individual product ROWS instead of per-year sums, which is the same wrong-aggregate mistake in miniature.) CONSEQUENCE: the blocker on iia magnitude verification is ITEM IDENTITY, not scale, and it is documented by iia-wheat-is-spelt-and-meslin and iia-item-series-switch-raw-products. The instruction above -- that iia assertions be verified on scope/vintage/documentary grounds only -- rests on refuted grounds and costs the 27 assertions this entry names, including its largest, serbia|iia|1920-1944 at 573 rows. STATUS LEFT AT pending_audit DELIBERATELY: refuting the evidence offered is not the same as proving iia magnitudes ARE on a common scale, which should rest on a positive test, and lifting a verifier instruction is a curation call.

label: (nested reporting levels; see summary)
summary: A polity can receive TWO OR MORE NESTING LEVELS of the same territory from the SAME source, so any aggregation over polity_code either sums a whole with its own parts or reads a cell that holds two incompatible values. Measured 2026-08-17 by routing all 189,839 matched layer-B rows through the assertion segments and grouping on (polity_code, source, item, indicator, year, unit): 52 such cells hold 110 rows contributed by more than one source label, and NONE of the colliding values are equal, so this is not duplicate ingestion but genuinely different series landing on one key. Worst cases: PNG-1949-1975 [fao1952] 18 rows from 'papua' + 'new guinea' (the two component territories FAO still reported separately after the 1949 union); CHN-1949-1950 13 rows and CHN-1947-1949 12 rows from 'china' + 'china 22 provinces' + 'china manchuria' (the 22-provinces rows are China proper EXCLUDING Manchuria: their land-use totals are 507,182 vs 106,930 thousand ha, i.e. ~5.07M km2 vs ~1.07M km2, so the two are disjoint components of the polity); FID-1887-1954 10 rows from 'indochina' + 'indochina viet nam'; KOR-1948-2025 10 rows from 'korea' + 'korea south'; DEU-1920-1938 9 rows from 'germany' + 'germany western' + 'germany berlin' for 1937 alone, which leaves the Reich polity carrying three mutually incompatible 1937 population values (Berlin's 4,284 thousand among them, against a Reich total near 67 million); JPN-1895-1945 [iia] 8 rows from 'japan' + 'palau'; GBR-1921-2025 8 rows from 'united kingdom' + 'united kingdom great britain' (Great Britain excludes Northern Ireland); CHN-1950-2025 6 rows; SER-1878-1913 [juan] 4 rows from 'serbia' + 'yugoslav sfr'; and 2 rows each on ETH-1907-1936/ETH-1936-1941/ETH-1941-1952 ('ethiopia' + 'ethiopia pdr'), PAL-1920-1948 ('israel' + 'palestine'), VGB-1800-2025 and ZAF-1910-2025 ('south africa' + 'natal'). Aggregate-level nesting without cell conflicts exists too and is not counted here (BWI-1833-1962 and BLI-1833-1960 beside their constituent islands; GCT-1919-1956 beside GHA-1898-1957 and BTL-1920-1957; PYF-1800-2025 beside 'makatea'; USA-1867-1959 beside 'alaska'/'guam'/'american samoa'/'virgin islands us'). This is the same hazard already recorded for one label in united-states-california-double-count, generalised and quantified. Audit required: decide, per family, which nesting level the polity represents, then either drop the other level (as the California row does) or give the component its own polity/segment. Fourteen legacy-tier assertions were quarantined rather than confirmed on this ground (see quarantine.csv, 2026-08-17); each names the missing segment where one exists: MAN-1945-1950 already covers 1945-1949 Manchuria, TNGU-1920-1949 and TPAP-1906-1949 end at the 1949 PNG union, BRL-1938-1945 and WZO-1938-1949 both start in 1938 so the 1937 Berlin and western-zone rows have no target, and the Caroline Islands have no polity for the 1914-1920 Japanese occupation (GCAR-1899-1914 -> CAR-1920-1945). No polity or polygon change is made here.

label: (16 labels; see summary)

China mainland 1940 reads 51,345,800 t and the Russian Federation 1936 reads 27,600,000 t, each an order of magnitude above the world total. 16 countries, all years 1934-1945: algeria, chile, china mainland, czech republic, indonesia, iran, japan, myanmar, philippines, russian federation, serbia, south korea, syrian arab republic, thailand, turkey, zimbabwe. The other 567 rows look fine -- median 5,200 t -- so this is NOT a blanket rescaling of iia tobacco. FACTOR: where the same country has an ADJACENT-YEAR value from another source, the ratio is about x100 and is tight: nine countries splice mitchell->iia at 1939->1940 with a median ratio of 101, and back DOWN by the same factor at the 1940->1941 return seam (japan 86,000 t in 1939, 8,705,400 in 1940, 84,000 in 1941). Do NOT read the per-row ratios against DISTANT comparison years as factor estimates -- serbia's apparent x469 to x1610 compares 1934-1945 iia against a 1910 juan value, a 25-year gap, and says nothing about the multiplier. The precise factor per row is not established; the implausibility is. This is a specific instance of iia-layerb-magnitude-scale-inconsistent, and the seam evidence is recorded in state/source_splices.csv and guarded by scripts/validate_source_splices.py. Consumers should treat these 40 cells as unusable rather than scaling them, since the factor is inferred from neighbours rather than known. FACTOR NOW ESTABLISHED (2026-08-18, superseding this entry's earlier caution). The entry previously said the per-row multiplier was NOT established and told consumers to drop these cells rather than rescale them, because no (country, year) overlap existed to measure a factor against. A polity-level cross-source comparison supplies one: different labels routing to the SAME polity make independent sources directly comparable (786 such cells exist; see issue #375). Measured there, iia is EXACTLY 100x another source -- within 0.5% -- on 22 tobacco cells: 18 against `juan` across F248-1920-1947, F51-1918-1938, F51-1938-1945 and F51-1945-1947 (1934-1945), and 4 against `mitchell` on KOR-1800-1945 (1935-1941). TWO INDEPENDENT SOURCES, FIVE POLITIES, SAME FACTOR, and the 1934-1945 window is exactly the one this entry already recorded. Examples: F248 1934 iia 604,900 vs juan 6,049; 1937 iia 2,078,300 vs juan 20,783; KOR 1934 iia 1,540,400 vs mitchell 15,000. So for a cell with a cross-source comparison the repair is division by 100. For the remaining cells in the affected set there is no comparison and the factor is INFERRED, not measured -- treat those as unusable rather than rescaling them blind. Note what has NOT changed: the earlier retraction of ranking rows by ratio-to-NEAREST-source stands, since that method produced serbia at 'x1610' by comparing 1934-1945 iia against a 1910 juan value. The factor is established by same-year comparison at the same polity, which is a different and sound measurement.

label: (28 series; worst listed in summary)
commodity: (multiple: sugar, p, n, grapes, wheat, cotton lint, raisins)
summary: A layer-B iia ITEM SERIES can be stitched from several DIFFERENT raw products, switching year to year, so its level shifts are product switches rather than changes in output. 28 series mix raw products whose levels differ by >=3x, each product supplying >=2 cells. The switches go BACK AND FORTH, which is what rules out growth as the explanation. CLEAREST CASE, australia / sugar raw centrifugal / tonnes, 33 cells: cane 131,961 t (1912) -> BEET 922 (1913, x0.01) -> beet through 1919 -> cane 165,616 (1920, x105) -> cane 297,700 (1921) -> BEET 2,829 (1922, x0.01) -> `sugar: cane, unrefined` 537,212 (1925, x175) -> cane through 1938 (783,200) -> BEET 6,400 (1939, x0.01) -> cane 611,300 (1944, x873). Australia's beet sugar industry was negligible, so 12 of the 33 cells are about 1/300 of the series they sit in. OTHERS: sweden p (superphosphate -> basic slag x0.08 -> superphosphate x28); japan n (calcium cyanamide with ammonium sulfate in 1919 x27 and 1933 x5); japan p x26; norway p x17; congo and niger cotton lint (cotton vs cotton: ginned, 8-11x); czech republic grapes (grapes: table vs vineyards: all vs grapes: wine vs vineyards: grapes+raisins -- five products in a 17-value series, 8 ha against 27,000 ha); australia/cyprus/japan/israel/turkey grapes; usa and australia raisins. WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: the source never changes, so 16_source_splices.py sees no seam; the values are plausible for the product they came from, so no magnitude screen fires; and the item name is constant, so nothing keyed on it notices. CONSEQUENCE: any trend, growth rate or level-shift reading of an affected series is measuring the yearbook's choice of table, not agriculture. This is the mechanism behind part of issue #360's level-shift confound. NOT REPAIRABLE by rescaling -- each cell needs re-attributing to its own item. See issue #378.

label: (12+ labels incl. argentina, australia, belgium, chile, egypt, japan)
summary: The layer-B iia item `flax fibre and tow` is MAJORITY LINSEED -- the seed, not the fibre -- even though a separate `linseed` item exists (377 rows). Flax gives two products from one plant and they are not interchangeable: linseed is an oilseed, flax fibre and tow is a textile fibre, and the quantities differ by orders of magnitude for the same country. Measured against the raw IIA extract with the raw label required to match the layer-B label: of 543 `flax fibre and tow` cells, 168 match raw `linseed` and 109 match raw `flax: fibre`; 58 match BOTH and are ambiguous. So 110 cells are unambiguously LINSEED against 51 unambiguously flax fibre -- the item carries more of the crop it is not named for. 19 OF THOSE CELLS ARE ALSO PRESENT UNDER THE LAYER-B `linseed` ITEM at the same label, year, value and unit, so one observation is counted twice and any oilseed or fibre aggregate summing both items double-counts them. Magnitude check that makes the direction obvious: argentina appears with 1,590,000 t (1933), 2,025,000 t (1934) and 2,059,000 ha (1935) under `flax fibre and tow`. Argentina was the world's largest LINSEED producer and grew essentially no flax fibre; world flax fibre output was on the order of 500,000 t in total, so these are linseed figures. Also affected: australia, belgium, bolivia, chile, egypt, japan, mexico, new zealand, sweden, turkey, uruguay. NOT REPAIRABLE BY RESCALING: each cell needs re-attributing to the correct item, and the 58 ambiguous cells cannot be attributed from the panel at all. HYPOTHESIS, NOT MEASURED: issue #360's worst source splice is `united states / flax fibre and tow / ha` at x1655 across a juan->mitchell boundary, and a linseed-vs-fibre switch would produce exactly that. I cannot test it, because the raw extract I have is IIA's and that splice is between two other sources. See issue #380.

label: France Germany; France Eastern; Western
summary: PROVEN BY ARITHMETIC: in fao1952's hemp-fibre table the labels `France Germany`, `France Eastern` and `Western` are GERMANY, GERMANY EASTERN and GERMANY WESTERN. The yearbook page listed France, then Germany with indented Eastern/Western sub-rows, and the extraction carried the preceding country name forward onto the sub-rows -- inconsistently, since `Western` kept no prefix. The proof is internal and needs no source page: `France Eastern` + `Western` = `France Germany` EXACTLY on both indicators for 1934-1938 -- production 2.9 + 1.2 = 4.1 (1000 t) and area 4.0 + 2.0 = 6.0 (1000 ha) -- which is the parent/child identity, and the table contains NO bare `Germany` label at all while carrying `France` separately at 3.9. A France-plus-Germany aggregate would not equal the sum of two German zones, and France's own row would not also be present. AFFECTED: 6 rows (2 per label). Small, but it is the only instance of this defect anywhere in the panel that can be settled from the numbers alone, so it is the template for the rest. WHAT THIS IS NOT: fao1952 encodes hierarchy by CONCATENATING parent and child, and that is normal and correct. `Germany Western` (254 rows), `China Taiwan` (143), `Korea South` (131), `Indochina Viet Nam` (109), `British Borneo Sarawak` (44) and `Libya Tripolitania` (37) are real parent-child labels; 46 labels share the surface pattern and 1,512 of their 1,567 rows are correctly assigned. The defect is only where the prefix is NOT a parent of the remainder -- `France Germany`, `Australia Fiji`, `Leeward Islands Trinidad and Tobago`, `Union of South Africa Zanzibar & Pemba` -- which takes geographic knowledge to tell apart and cannot be detected from the label shape. About 55 rows in total. See issue #29.

label: czech republic; serbia
commodity: rye; flax fibre and tow; rapeseed
summary: 13 INDIVIDUALLY ATTRIBUTABLE defective cells, and unlike almost everything else in this file they are REPAIRABLE, because the correct value is known. Method: two labels that route to the same polity make two sources directly comparable; where they agree to within 1% on 70%+ of at least 8 shared years, they demonstrably measure the same thing, so a cell where they diverge by more than 2x is the defect rather than a difference of scope -- and the agreeing side supplies the value. A bare ratio cannot do this: it tells you two sources disagree, not which is wrong. iia `czech republic` vs juan `czechoslovakia`: rye (ha) 19/23 years agree, diverging 1939 (iia 98,000 vs juan 984,000), 1940 (78,000 vs 708,000), 1941 (78,000 vs 784,000), 1943 (26,000 vs 926,000); rye (tonnes) 18/23 agree, diverging 1942 (29,500 vs 1,231,000), 1943 (36,000 vs 1,536,000), 1944 (32,500 vs 1,214,000), 1945 (28,000 vs 981,000); flax fibre and tow (ha) 20/23 agree, diverging 1942 only (4,000 vs 43,000). iia `serbia` vs juan `yugoslav sfr`: rye (ha) 15/17 agree, diverging 1931 (24,415 vs 244,150) and 1932 (24,296 vs 242,961) -- both EXACTLY one tenth, 244,150/10 = 24,415 and 242,961/10 = 24,296.1; rye (tonnes) 17/18 agree, diverging 1945 where iia is the LARGER side (979,900 vs 92,000); rapeseed (tonnes) 15/16 agree, diverging 1920 (1,929 vs 3,900, x2.0). SHAPE: most divergences are near-exact powers of ten in one direction or the other, i.e. dropped or added digits in single cells, not a systematic rescaling -- the surrounding years match to the digit (czech rye 1930: iia 1,046,335 vs juan 1,046,335 exactly). The czech rye TONNES block 1942-1945 is the exception at x35-43 and is not a clean digit shift. NOT ESTABLISHED: which side is wrong in each case. The agreeing years prove the two measure one thing; they do not prove the majority is right. For czech rye the juan values are plausible for Czechoslovak rye (~700k-1M ha) and iia's 26,000-98,000 ha are not, so iia is the defective side there. serbia rye 1945 runs the other way and iia is the implausible one at 979,900 t. Each cell needs that check before it is repaired. CORRECTED 2026-08-18, SAME DAY: the 'dropped or added digits' reading above is WRONG for the czech cells, and so is the scope-flipping reading queued for the F51-1938-1945 wiki page. Inspecting the raw IIA extract directly, the `czechoslovakia` 1938-1945 block is internally corrupt: for RYE, either the area or the production value is implausible in 7 of the 8 years, and a yield check says which. 1938 reads 1,016,000 ha / 1,906,100 t = 1.88 t/ha, consistent. 1939 reads 98,000 ha / 1,729,400 t = 17.6 t/ha, so the AREA is the wrong cell. 1942 reads 861,000 ha / 29,500 t = 0.03 t/ha, so the PRODUCTION is the wrong cell; likewise 1944 (915,000 / 32,500) and 1945 (802,000 / 28,000). 1943 reads 26,000 ha / 36,000 t, internally consistent at 1.38 t/ha but both figures far too small for Czechoslovak rye. So the defective values are not digit-shifted versions of the truth -- they are numbers attached to the wrong (item, variable) slot in the extraction, which is why the two sides of the same year disagree with each other and not just with juan. The scope-flipping explanation is separately REFUTED: raw `german bohemia and moravia` exists but carries only butter, cheese and milk (21 rows, 1939-1945) and NO rye, so there is no sub-component rye series for the label to alternate with. Same block, same shape, other items: `tobacco` 1939 reads 6,000 ha with 933,000 t, and `hops` 1939 reads 10,500 ha with 763,400 t -- both the x100 defect already logged as iia-tobacco-implausible-magnitudes and iia-hops-x100. And the czech `flax fibre and tow` 1942 cell (4,000 vs juan's 43,000) is NOT a digit drop either: raw carries `flax: fibre` area 43,000 and `linseed` area 4,000 for 1942, so layer B took the LINSEED figure -- the conflation already logged as iia-flax-fibre-item-is-mostly-linseed. WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED: the serbia cells. 1931 (24,415 vs 244,150) and 1932 (24,296 vs 242,961) are still exact tenths, and no area/production misalignment is involved. The method also survives -- cross-source agreement on the surrounding years is what made these cells attributable at all -- but attributing them to a digit shift was reading a mechanism off a ratio.

summary: RESOLVES issue #360's two largest recorded source seams, and NOT by the mechanism that issue proposed. `united states / flax fibre and tow / ha` jumps x1655 at a juan->mitchell boundary and Canada x1231; #360 offered a unit or thousands-multiplier mismatch as the leading candidate. Proof is exact equality with juan's own separately-labelled linseed series for the same country: united states 1950 mitchell flax-fibre 1,655,000 ha == juan linseed 1,655,000; 1952 mitchell 1,337,000 == juan 1,337,000; 1900 and 1901 likewise. canada 1952 mitchell 469,000 == juan linseed 469,000 (at 1951, the crop-year offset). Across the whole panel, 55 of the 204 mitchell `flax fibre and tow` (ha) values exactly equal a juan LINSEED (ha) value for the same country, against just 1 of 204 that equals a juan FLAX FIBRE AND TOW value -- a 55:1 ratio against the control, which rules out coincidence as the account of the bulk. Some of the 55 sit at a +/-1 year offset, which is the southern-hemisphere crop-year convention (argentina mitchell 1911 == juan 1912, and so on through 1922). THE YIELD IDENTITY CORROBORATES INDEPENDENTLY. juan's US flax-fibre series runs 3,000 ha and 1,900 t (1945) down to 1,000 ha and 400 t (1949), i.e. 0.30-0.63 t/ha, which is fibre flax. Mitchell's 1,655,000 ha against juan's 1950 fibre production of 100 t would imply 0.00006 t/ha. US linseed yields 0.46-0.70 t/ha across the same years, which is what these areas belong to. SCOPE: this is the same conflation already logged as iia-flax-fibre-item-is-mostly-linseed, now shown to affect MITCHELL as well as IIA -- so it is a property of how the item was harmonised rather than of one source. Not repairable by rescaling: the affected cells need re-attributing to `linseed`, and 27% is a floor on the share affected rather than an estimate, because it counts only cells whose value survives to be matched exactly.

A NEGATIVE RESULT FROM THE SAME SEARCH, recorded so it is not repeated: scanning all raw labels for an earliest year separated from the body by >=5 years with <=5 rows in the head returns FIVE candidates and only this one is a defect. `china` [1914], `china: manchuria` [1915-17], `french guiana` [1909-13] and `french west africa` [1918-19] all carry plausible values for territories that existed in those years -- so time-isolation is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, and convicting a case needs the label's founding date, which is curation rather than measurement.
